page: Oracle Cloud Infrastructure VM.Standard.E6.Flex.32-256 is a standard general-purpose cloud instance built on the x86_64 CPU architecture. The server is equipped with AMD EPYC 9J45 processors operating at a clock frequency of 2.7 GHz. Computational resources are partitioned into 32 dedicated physical cores, which provide 64 virtual central processing units via two hardware threads per core. Memory capacity is provisioned at 256 GB of RAM, adhering to a uniform memory distribution of 4.0 GB per physical core or 4.0 GB per vCPU ratio across the instance.

The instance does not incorporate bundled local storage, requiring persistent operational disks and scratch space to be provisioned via network block storage volumes. Similarly, the VM.Standard.E6.Flex.32-256 contains zero discrete GPU accelerators, orienting its operational scope strictly toward CPU-driven execution paths. Network-facing configuration includes one complimentary public IPv4 address for external routing and remote administrative access. Dedicated CPU scheduling prevents noisy neighbor interference, ensuring consistent execution cycles across all 64 vCPUs.

Because of its balanced core-to-memory density, this instance offers high resource efficiency for horizontally and vertically scaled general-purpose applications without paying a premium for unused memory or specialized acceleration hardware. The VM.Standard.E6.Flex.32-256 is appropriate for production web backends, enterprise middleware, containerized application clusters, continuous integration and build pipelines, batch data processing jobs, and relational or caching database deployments.
description: Oracle Cloud Infrastructure VM.Standard.E6.Flex.32-256 is a general-purpose virtual machine configuration based on the x86_64 architecture. Powered by dedicated AMD EPYC 9J45 processors running at a base clock speed of 2.7 GHz, this instance provisions 32 physical cores supporting two threads per core for a total of 64 dedicated vCPUs. It incorporates 256 GB of system memory, maintaining a standard general-purpose allocation of 4.0 GB per core. The server configuration includes one complimentary public IPv4 address and does not provide bundled local storage or discrete GPU accelerators, relying on external network volumes for filesystem storage. The balanced allocation of processing threads and memory capacity provides consistent multi-threaded compute capacity without resource oversubscription. This server profile is suited for general enterprise application hosting, distributed microservices, continuous integration pipelines, batch data transformations, and relational databases.
